guide.title: Build a learning session with Learn.
guide.lead: Prepare a task, choose the kind of help, send learner work and read saved results. Interface version `2026-12-01`.
guide.intro: Learn uses the existing `/v1/quest` endpoints, `quest` request fields and `quest_receipt` events. Use these names exactly as documented below; existing integrations remain compatible.

sections.title: Get the right access
sections.markdown:
## Get the right access

Self-service access is for adults in the United States and Canada, excluding Quebec. Education and uses involving children are set up under an agreement.

[Add Learn to your workspace](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/apis/learn/#pricing) with test or live access. Sign-in, terms and workspace selection preserve the selected product. Enrollment creates no key and starts no generation. Private or older assignments keep their own release and rate.

Try [Learn in the Sandbox](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/sandbox/learn/) with your signed-in account. For your application, create a scoped server key in My APIs. Keep it on your backend; browsers call your own authenticated backend. Send a [pseudonymous learner id](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#learner-id) in `X-User-Id`, the assigned `X-Assignment-Id`, and use the correct environment’s API host.

Use synthetic data in staging. Your application owns consent, oversight and escalation. Learn does not grade, and it does not guarantee correctness. Diagnostic describes what a learner’s work shows about their understanding; it is not a clinical assessment.

sections.title: Prepare without generating
Name the tutor
sections.markdown:
## Name the tutor

`setup.display_name` is the name the tutor uses for itself. A session prepared with `"display_name": "Maple"` opens with “I am Maple.” Leave the field out, or send `null`, and the tutor is Learn.

The name can be up to 80 characters. It is set when the session is prepared and stays for that session. Square brackets, angle brackets and control characters are refused with a 400. The name changes how the tutor introduces itself, not what it is: your product still tells learners they are working with an AI tutor.

sections.title: Describe the learner
sections.markdown:
## Describe the learner

`setup.learner` tells Learn who it is teaching. Every field is optional.

| Field | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `grade_band` | `primary`, `middle`, `9-10`, `11-12`, `higher_education`, `adult`, `unspecified` |
| `reading_level` | `on_grade`, `simplified`, `unspecified` |
| `support_needs` | `none`, `step_by_step`, `plain_language`, `unspecified` |
| `language` | `en`. Replies are in US English. |
| `preferred_name` | Up to 80 characters. How the tutor addresses the learner; leave it out and the tutor uses no name. |

```json
{
  "learner": {
    "grade_band": "middle",
    "reading_level": "simplified",
    "support_needs": "step_by_step",
    "language": "en"
  }
}
```

Learn sets its pace and vocabulary from the grade band, the reading level and the support needs together. The grade band also travels with every turn, so safety responses suit the learner’s age group. There is no age field: send the grade band that fits the learner, from `primary` to `adult`.

sections.title: Give each learner a pseudonymous id
sections.markdown:
## Give each learner a pseudonymous id

`X-User-Id` identifies the learner. Make it a pseudonym your product controls: a random id that you store against your own user record. Never send a name, an email address or a student number.

Keep it stable. Saved learning records and memory belong to the id, so a new id is a new learner to Learn. Use one id per learner, also when several learners share one thread in your product.

An id is 1 to 200 characters with no control characters. Ids are scoped to your workspace and assignment. The console’s Sandbox keeps its own separate set of test users. To remove a learner, [erase by id](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#privacy).

sections.title: Four kinds of help
sections.markdown:
## Four kinds of help

| Kind | What the learner gets | How you choose it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `diagnostic` | What they actually understand, with the evidence, from work they have already finished. | `setup.posture` when you [prepare the session](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#diagnostic). |

Guided, Feedback and Explain are chosen on each request. Leaving `posture` out of a teaching request means Guided every time, including after Feedback or Explain; a client can remember its selected kind and send it explicitly. Diagnostic is chosen when the session is prepared, and that session stays Diagnostic when `posture` is left out. There is no answer-only mode.

`quest.requested_support` accepts `auto`, `hint`, `framework`, `example` or `coaching`. It requests support without overriding learning safeguards. Do not send privileged instructions, model settings, replacement memory or raw internal state.

sections.title: Run a Diagnostic session
sections.markdown:
## Run a Diagnostic session

Diagnostic looks at work a learner has already finished, such as a quiz or a problem set, and finds what explains it. Prepare a session of its own with `setup.posture: "diagnostic"` and put the finished work in `setup.assessment`. Send the work as text in a source, or [upload a photo](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#files) first and put its `attachment_id` in a source with an empty `text`.

Save this as `diagnostic-setup.json`. Every field of `assessment` is required; `items`, `targets` and `limitations` may be empty lists and `original_result` may be an empty string.

```json
{
  "setup": {
    "task": {
      "kind": "practice",
      "subject": "Fractions",
      "assignment": "Review a finished five-question quiz on adding fractions."
    },
    "learner": {
      "grade_band": "middle",
      "language": "en"
    },
    "posture": "diagnostic",
    "assessment": {
      "schema_version": "fl.quest.assessment-input.v1",
      "goal": "How the learner adds fractions with unlike denominators.",
      "sources": [
        {
          "id": "finished-work",
          "origin": "submitted_work",
          "text": "1) 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4\n2) 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5\n3) 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5\n4) 1/3 + 1/6 = 2/9\n5) 3/4 + 1/8 = 4/12",
          "attachment_id": null,
          "locator": "Finished quiz supplied as text",
          "availability": "available"
        }
      ],
      "items": [],
      "targets": [],
      "original_result": "",
      "limitations": []
    }
  }
}
```

```
diagnostic-opening.json
{"session_id":"<returned-session-id>","prompt":"","quest":{"operation":"opening"}}

diagnostic-reply.json
{"session_id":"<returned-session-id>","prompt":"I added the tops, then I added the bottoms.","quest":{"operation":"turn"}}
```

```sh
H=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY" -H "X-Assignment-Id: $FOREVERLEARNING_ASSIGNMENT_ID" \
   -H "X-User-Id: synthetic-learner-1" -H "FL-API-Version: 2026-12-01")
J=(-H "Content-Type: application/json")

# 1. Prepare the session. Free. Save the returned session_id as $SESSION.
curl "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/quest/sessions" "${H[@]}" "${J[@]}" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $PREPARE_OPERATION_ID" --data-binary @diagnostic-setup.json

# 2. Request the opening. One turn. Leave posture out.
curl --no-buffer "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/chat" "${H[@]}" "${J[@]}" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $OPENING_OPERATION_ID" --data-binary @diagnostic-opening.json

# 3. Send each learner reply. One turn each. Leave posture out.
curl --no-buffer "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/chat" "${H[@]}" "${J[@]}" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $REPLY_OPERATION_ID" --data-binary @diagnostic-reply.json

# 4. End the session. One turn. end.json holds {"operation_id": "<the same UUID as its Idempotency-Key>"}.
curl --no-buffer -X POST "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/sessions/$SESSION/end" "${H[@]}" "${J[@]}" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $END_OPERATION_ID" --data-binary @end.json

# 5. Read the report. Free.
curl "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/quest/sessions/$SESSION/assessment" "${H[@]}"
```

In a Diagnostic session Learn asks the learner how they worked. It does not teach and it does not give answers. There is no fixed number of questions: your product ends the session when it chooses, and the report covers what was examined by then. Validate each response exactly as you [validate any turn](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#turn).

### Read the result

`GET /v1/quest/sessions/ID/assessment` returns the report. Its `state` is `active` while the session is open. After the session ends it is `closed` and `frozen` is true: the report no longer changes. `current` holds what to show:

- `findings`: each has a `kind` (`skill`, `gap`, `misconception` or `unassessed`), a `title`, an `observation`, an `interpretation`, a `qualification` (`supported`, `provisional` or `unresolved`) and the `evidence_refs` it rests on.
- `result_evidence`: each answer Learn checked, with an `outcome` (`correct`, `incorrect`, `indeterminate` or `no_answer`) and its `judgment`.
- `diagnosis`, `coverage`, `limitations` and `unanswered_questions`: the overall reading, what it covers and what it leaves open.

`events` lists what was recorded turn by turn, and `input` returns the work you supplied. Show a finding with its qualification and evidence, not as a grade.

sections.title: Upload learner work separately
sections.markdown:
## Upload learner work separately

`POST /v1/quest/attachments` accepts one file as `media_type`, plain base64 `data`, optional `filename` and optional `session_id`. Save the upload’s idempotency key before dispatch. Use the opaque returned `attachment_id` in an ordinary turn.

| Input | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| PNG, JPEG, WebP | 8 MiB per image; 6,000 pixels per side; 36 million pixels |
| UTF-8 text or Markdown | 64 KiB per file |
| Files on a turn | Four handles total |

Files are scoped to workspace, assignment, environment, region and learner. A session-bound upload cannot move to another session. Expiry is fixed at 30 days from upload; reads and reuse do not extend it. Limits are 32 retained uploads and 64 MiB per learner, 256 MiB per workspace/environment, and 100 uploads per learner in a rolling day.

Use legible, relevant work. PDF, SVG, external file URLs and data URLs are not accepted. Handles cannot accompany legacy inline `images`, opening, closeout or slash commands. Older inline-image clients retain their separate three-image, 8 MiB aggregate bound.

Uploading is free. `GET /v1/quest/attachments/ID` requires `sessions:read`; deletion is idempotent. Export-only retrieval uses `POST /v1/quest/data/export/attachments/ID` and `data:export`. Neither route creates a public file URL.

sections.title: Send a turn and validate its result
sections.markdown:
## Send a turn and validate its result

Save the following body as `saved-turn.json`, substituting returned IDs. Omit `attachment_ids` entirely for a text-only turn. Use one saved operation UUID per new operation. Set the base URL to your assigned host ending in `/v1`.

```json
{
  "session_id": "<returned-session-id>",
  "prompt": "Help me check the steps in my work.",
  "posture": "feedback",
  "quest": {
    "operation": "turn",
    "requested_support": "auto",
    "team_dialog": false,
    "attachment_ids": [
      "<uploaded-attachment-id>"
    ]
  }
}
```

```sh
curl --no-buffer "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/chat" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Assignment-Id: $FOREVERLEARNING_ASSIGNMENT_ID" \
  -H "X-User-Id: synthetic-learner-1" \
  -H "FL-API-Version: 2026-12-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $SAVED_OPERATION_ID" \
  --data-binary @saved-turn.json
```

This cURL snippet shows the request. The runnable examples below also validate completion. Prompts allow up to 10,000 UTF-16 code units. The response is a server-sent event stream. Its events arrive in this order:

```json
{"type":"metadata","sessionId":"...","request_id":"..."}
{"type":"content","part":"conversation","text":"..."}
{"type":"content","part":"display","text":"..."}
{"type":"content","part":"frame","text":"..."}        only when team dialog is on for the turn
{"type":"display_complete"}
{"type":"safety_status","schema_version":1,"evaluated":true,"level":"clear","response_action":"none","source":"governed_turn"}
{"type":"quest_receipt","receipt":{"mode":"...","posture":"guided","composition_hash":"...","turn_index":1,"team_dialog":false,"repairs":[],"validation_failures":[]}}
{"type":"session_ended","sessionId":"..."}             only on a closeout
{"type":"done","sessionId":"...","stopReason":"end_turn","commercial":{"billable_units":1,"charge":{"amount_micro_usd":50000,"currency":"USD"},"settlement":"...","request_id":"...","listing":"...","band":"...","rate_version":"..."}}
{"type":"error","error":true,"code":"...","message":"...","request_id":"..."}   in place of done, when the response began but could not finish
```

Do not treat HTTP 200 or received text as committed success.

1. Save the `metadata` request and session identity.
2. Render `content` separately by `conversation` and `display` part, using safe text, Markdown, math and code rendering. Read parts by their `part` value, not by position.
3. Validate the [safety status](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#safety) and the closed `quest_receipt`. The receipt identifies the kind of help and the serving composition; it is not a learning assessment.
4. Require final `done` with matching session/request identity and the original commercial result. For closeout, also require `session_ended`.

Unknown future events do not replace required completion. Never expose raw internal frames, parse hidden carriers from text or treat an unverified preview as saved output. A safety result of unknown is not an all-clear.

A request that fails before its response begins answers with JSON instead of events; see [When a request is refused](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#errors). Once the response has begun, a failure arrives as an `error` event in place of `done`, with `code`, `message` and the `request_id`, and no `done` follows. Read `GET /v1/requests/REQUEST_ID` for the outcome: a turn that failed is not charged, and a saved turn returns its result and receipt. In test mode, a request uses one free attempt once Learn starts generating its reply, whether it then succeeds or fails; Learn’s internal retry and a replay add nothing.

sections.title: Read the safety status on every turn
sections.markdown:
## Read the safety status on every turn

Every turn carries one `safety_status` event. It arrives after the content and `display_complete`, before `quest_receipt` and `done`.

| `level` | What Learn’s reply does | `response_action` | What your product does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clear` | The lesson goes on. | `none` | Nothing extra. |
| `watch` | It asks what the student means. | `support` | Show the reply as it is. Keep your support path within reach. |
| `warning` | It takes it seriously, at once. | `support` | Show the reply as it is. Bring your human support path forward. |
| `critical` | It asks for someone they trust, now, and says where to get immediate help. | `support` | Show the reply at once, as it is. Offer your product’s human escalation path and follow your own reporting duties. |
| `unknown` | Safety was not evaluated for this turn; `evaluated` is false. | `none` | Unknown is never clear. Do not show an all-clear; keep your usual support path visible. |

`evaluated` is false only for `unknown`. `source` is `governed_turn` when the status comes from the reply itself, and `backstop` when a fallback check ran because the reply could not be read; the backstop reports only `critical` or `unknown`. The contract also defines the action `escalate`. This release sends `none` or `support`; if you receive `escalate`, handle it as you handle `critical`.

### Your product’s part in a crisis

Show the reply as Learn wrote it. Never hide it, delay it or replace it with your own text. Offer your product’s own human escalation path beside it. Do not present Learn as an emergency service or as monitored by a person in real time. An absent signal is not an assurance of safety.

At the highest level the reply can name crisis resources in the United States, including emergency services and the 988 line. Learn is not told where a learner is: if you serve learners in Canada, show your local resources beside the reply.

When the safety check on a learner’s message flags self-harm, that turn is free. It is answered even when your balance has run out, and it uses no free attempt. The rule follows the check on the message, not the level in the reply, so read the charge from `done`; do not infer it from the level.

### The optional safety webhook

In the console you can opt in to signed safety events sent to your own server. Give a public HTTPS endpoint on port 443, without credentials, query strings or redirects, and store the signing secret the console shows once. Each event carries the safety status and opaque identifiers, never conversation text or the learner’s id; verify its `X-FL-Signature` header before you act on it. Delivery runs apart from the turn: a slow or failed delivery never holds back or changes the reply.

sections.title: Show the team behind the turn
sections.markdown:
## Show the team behind the turn

Learn has a team behind every turn. Set `team_dialog: true` when you prepare the session, or override it for one request with `quest.team_dialog`, and the response can also carry the team’s exchange as `content` events with `part: "frame"`.

Show frame text only when the verified receipt has `team_dialog: true`, and show it apart from the reply to the learner: the `conversation` and `display` parts are the reply, the `frame` part is the team. Team dialog is always off in a Diagnostic session.

sections.title: Keep the receipt
Design the wait
sections.markdown:
## Design the wait

Learn checks every reply before it releases it. The reply therefore arrives whole, near the end of the request, not word by word. Show a working state from the moment you send, and keep the connection open until `done`.

In our testing on this release a reply reached the client about 10 to 20 seconds after the request, and an opening took about as long. An opening that first closes [an earlier open session](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#open-session) took about 19 seconds. Nothing arrives early: the response itself begins when the reply is ready, so set client and proxy timeouts well above these times. If the connection drops while you wait, [recover the request](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#recovery); do not send it again under a new key.

sections.title: Read committed learning records
sections.markdown:
## Read committed learning records

List paginated sessions with `GET /v1/quest/sessions`. Read setup and status with `GET /v1/quest/sessions/ID`, latest state at `/state`, and saved closeout at `/summary`. The learner’s profile is `GET /v1/quest/learners/USER_ID/profile`; its path must match the authenticated learner. A Diagnostic session’s report is at `/assessment`.

To remember a learner between visits, four reads are enough: the session list, then the state and summary of the session you resume from, and the profile. A learner with no sessions yet gets an empty list, not an error.

State includes saved progress, the kind of help, effective support when known, observed signals and source turn/time. Profile separates supplied preferences from observed signals and support history. Empty evidence stays null or unavailable. These reads never generate observations, grades, diagnoses or mastery percentages.

We never train an AI model on learners’ data, and never share it with an AI company to train theirs.

Finish through `POST /v1/sessions/ID/end` with a durable `operation_id` and matching idempotency key. Successful closeout saves the summary. A prepared session can be discarded without buying an opening. Generic session history and request recovery keep their existing scoped routes.

sections.title: Starting a new session while an earlier one is open
sections.markdown:
## Starting a new session while an earlier one is open

A learner has one active session at a time on an assignment. The first turn of the learner’s next session, its opening or the learner’s first message, closes the open one with a closeout, charged as a closeout (5¢), the same as ending it yourself. Preparing a session closes nothing. Ending is optional: call `POST /v1/sessions/ID/end` when you want the summary right away.

If you start a new session for a learner whose earlier session was never ended, Learn closes the earlier session for you first: it runs that session’s closeout, which saves its summary and memory, and then opens the new session.

Two things follow. The closeout is billed as its own request at your normal rate, and it appears in Usage as a separate charged request made just before your opening. The opening also takes longer, about ten seconds more in our testing, because two replies are generated.

The opening’s reply says nothing about the earlier session; read the earlier session afterward with `GET /v1/quest/sessions/ID/summary` to see its summary. If the earlier session’s closeout fails Learn’s checks, the new session still opens: the earlier one is closed without a summary, and its turns stay readable. To avoid the extra wait at a moment you did not choose, end a session with `POST /v1/sessions/ID/end` when the learner finishes.

sections.title: Recover the original operation
sections.markdown:
## Recover the original operation

Preserve assignment, learner, session, body and idempotency key after a disconnect. Retry exactly those inputs or read `GET /v1/requests/REQUEST_ID`. A changed body with the same key conflicts. Do not rotate the key because a connection failed.

`in_progress` means check again; `unavailable` is not a confirmed failure or permission for another purchase. A committed result must pass the same receipt checks as the original response. The runtime has one bounded internal retry; it creates no second customer charge and uses no second free attempt.

After a turn that failed and was not charged, the same key returns `409 REQUEST_FAILED`. That answer is final for the key: send the turn again with a new idempotency key. Only this confirmed failure permits a new request for the same learner message.

`GET /v1/requests/REQUEST_ID` finds only a request that was accepted, and only when you read it with the same API key, assignment and `X-User-Id`. A request that was [refused](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#errors) at the door was never accepted, so there is nothing to recover: fix the cause and send it again with a new idempotency key. Looking up an id that names no accepted request answers `404 DEVELOPER_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND`.

When an accepted request fails before its response begins, the refusal’s `request_id` is that request’s own id, so `GET /v1/requests/REQUEST_ID` reads it.

Respect an actual `Retry-After` header. Resolve authentication and scopes for 401/403, balance or funding for 402, original operation/conflict for 409, and allowance or rate limits for 429. Do not infer free retries with new identities.

sections.title: When a request is refused
sections.markdown:
## When a request is refused

A refused request answers with JSON. Four fields are always present: `error` (true), `code`, `message` and `request_id`. Decide by the HTTP status and `code`, not by the message text, and keep `request_id` for support.

Some refusals also say what to fix. These fields are optional, and a client should ignore any field it does not know.

| Field | Sent on | What it tells you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | 429 | Which limit was reached: `requests_per_minute`, `concurrent_streams` (replies in progress at once), `daily_limit` or `new_users_daily`. |
| `retry_after_seconds` | 429 | Seconds until a retry can succeed, when a truthful time exists. The `Retry-After` header carries the same number. |
| `field` | 400 | The request field to fix, as a path of the contract’s field names: for example `setup.task.kind` or `quest.operation`, `body` for the whole body, `header:X-User-Id` or `query:limit`. It is never a value you sent, and an unknown field is reported by its parent. |
| `issue` | 400 | What is wrong with that field: `missing`, `unknown_field`, `wrong_type`, `too_long`, `too_short`, `too_large`, `invalid_value`, `not_allowed_here` or `malformed`. `not_allowed_here` means the field is valid but not accepted on this request or at this point in the session. |
| `scope` | 429 | Whose limit it is: `key`, `workspace` or `service`. It is in the contract and is not sent yet. |

### The codes you will meet

| Status and code | What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 `DEVELOPER_INVALID_REQUEST` | The request is not valid. | Fix the field named by `field` and `issue` when they are present, then send it again. |
| 400 `DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_REQUIRED` | Diagnostic was asked for on a session that was not prepared for it. | Create the session with `setup.posture` set to `diagnostic` and the finished work, then open it. See [Run a Diagnostic session](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#diagnostic). |
| 401 `DEVELOPER_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` | The request was not authenticated. | Send your server key as a Bearer token, to the API host of the right environment. |
| 402 `DEVELOPER_BALANCE_EXHAUSTED`, `KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` | The workspace balance, or the key’s budget, is used up. | Add balance, or raise the key’s budget, in the console. |
| 403 `DEVELOPER_OPERATION_REFUSED` | The request is not permitted. Many causes share this one answer, [on purpose](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#errors-generic). | Check the key’s scopes, the assignment, the session id and the `X-User-Id`. |
| 403 `DEVELOPER_POLICY_BLOCKED` | The safety screening refused the learner’s message before it reached the tutor. | Show your own short message and let the learner continue. See [below](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#errors-policy). |
| 403 `DEVELOPER_WORKLOAD_REVIEW_REQUIRED` | New replies on this API are paused while ForeverLearning renews its routine review of the API’s serving costs, such as its price review. Nothing was charged and no free attempt was used. | Nothing in your request needs to change. ForeverLearning renews the review; send the request again later with a new idempotency key. |
| 404 `DEVELOPER_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` | A [request lookup](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#recovery) found no request with that id for this learner. | Look it up with the same API key, assignment and `X-User-Id` as the request. A request refused at the door was never accepted: send it again with a new idempotency key. |
| 409 `REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS`, `REQUEST_FAILED` | The original request is still running, or it failed and was not charged. | [Recover the request](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#recovery): check again while it runs; after a confirmed failure, send it again with a new idempotency key. |
| 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` | The idempotency key was already used for a different request. | Send the original body with that key, or use a new key for a new request. |
| 429 `DEVELOPER_CAPACITY_LIMIT` | A limit on requests was reached. `reason` says which. | Wait for `retry_after_seconds` when it is present. For `concurrent_streams`, wait for your own replies in progress to finish. |
| 429 `DEVELOPER_NEW_USER_LIMIT` | The day’s limit on end users seen for the first time was reached. End users already admitted are not affected. | Keep serving the learners you already have. New end users can start after 00:00 UTC; `Retry-After` counts to that time. |
| 503 `DEVELOPER_WORKSPACE_NOT_READY` | The workspace is not ready to admit new end users. | Contact ForeverLearning with the `request_id`. Sending it again does not help. |
| 503 `DEVELOPER_UNAVAILABLE` | The service is temporarily unavailable. | Send the same request again later with its original idempotency key. |

### Retry-After

On a 429 that has a truthful retry time, the `Retry-After` header and `retry_after_seconds` carry the same number of seconds: 60 for `requests_per_minute`, and the seconds to the next 00:00 UTC for `daily_limit` and `new_users_daily`. `concurrent_streams` carries none, because it clears when your own replies finish. `DEVELOPER_SANDBOX_LIMIT` and `DEVELOPER_MISUSE_COOLDOWN` carry none either. A retry time appears only on a 429.

### What stays the same on purpose

An unknown session, a closed session and another end user’s session all answer `403 DEVELOPER_OPERATION_REFUSED`, byte for byte the same. So do an unavailable key, assignment, organization or account, and an operation the key may not perform. This is deliberate: a more specific answer would tell a caller whether a session id exists, or whose it is. These answers never carry the optional fields or a `Retry-After` header. In the same way, a request lookup answers `404 DEVELOPER_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` alike for an id that does not exist and for another end user’s request.

### When a learner’s message is refused

A message refused with `403 DEVELOPER_POLICY_BLOCKED` was stopped by the safety screening before it reached the tutor. Show your own short message, for example “I can’t help with that message. Try asking another way.”, and let the learner continue. Do not show the refusal’s own text to a learner.

sections.title: Export, delete and erase deliberately
sections.markdown:
## Export, delete and erase deliberately

`POST /v1/quest/data/export` returns paginated sessions, profile and attachment inventory with `data:export`. Follow every `next_cursor`; download each retained attachment separately. Generic `POST /v1/data/export` includes message history. Reads do not extend retention.

Deleting a file removes its bytes while preserving committed financial/turn receipts. Discard removes session content and unshared files. `POST /v1/data/erase` erases the learner named by `X-User-Id`, using the existing learner-erasure authority and `data:erase`; preserve its operation identity until completion is confirmed. Financial records required for accounting remain.

The console’s Sandbox user namespace is separate from your API integration’s users. Select the correct namespace for export and erasure. Upload previews and file bytes must not be persisted in browser operation storage. Text retention follows the assigned lifecycle: test content expires after 30 days of inactivity, live content after 180; uploads retain their fixed 30-day expiry.

sections.title: What counts as a turn
sections.markdown:
## What counts as a turn

Learn is priced per turn, not per seat: 5¢ per turn that succeeds. A turn that fails costs nothing. Fifty free attempts in every workspace.

| 5¢ each, when it succeeds | Free |
| --- | --- |
| A reply to a learner’s message, with any attached work included.A session’s opening, when you request one.A session’s closeout, including the closeout Learn runs for you when a [new session starts while an earlier one is open](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/#open-session). | A turn that fails.A turn whose learner message the safety check flags for self-harm.Preparing a session.Uploading work.Reading saved records, including a Diagnostic report.Learn’s own internal retry, and replaying a request with its original key. |

A Diagnostic session costs what its turns cost: the opening, each learner reply and the closeout. One with two learner replies is four turns, 20¢. Read your assignment’s price from `GET /v1/quest/catalog`; My APIs and the original receipt identify the rate for an existing assignment.

The fifty free attempts are for test access. They last for the life of the workspace and are shared across its members and keys. A dispatched failure and a generated closeout each use an attempt; the internal retry and a replay do not. Reenrollment or a new release does not reset them. Save an attempt for closeout. Running out never switches on live charging by itself.

examples.text:
# Learn server examples

Use a scoped Learn server key and an assignment in the same environment. The browser Sandbox uses your signed-in account instead. These examples require Node 24+ for TypeScript and intent preparation; Python 3.11+ is an independent standard-library transport. The cURL example uses Python for the same intent and receipt checks. No package installation is needed.

Set `FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY` on your server, `FOREVERLEARNING_ASSIGNMENT_ID`, and a stable pseudonymous `FOREVERLEARNING_USER_ID` (this example accepts letters, digits, underscores and hyphens). Set `FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL` to your assigned host ending in `/v1`; preparation defaults to staging. Never put a server key in browser code or commit it. Use synthetic data in staging.

Prepare a request once, then send that saved file with one transport:

```sh
node prepare.mjs setup setup.intent.json
node quest.ts setup.intent.json setup.response.json
# Equivalent transports, using the SAME saved intent:
python quest.py setup.intent.json setup-python.response.json
bash quest.sh setup.intent.json setup-curl.response.json
```

Setup returns `data.session_id` without generating an answer or using a trial attempt. Save that identity as `SESSION_ID`. Each command below prepares a distinct explicit operation. Do not run a preparation command again to recover a disconnected request. Output files must be new so a later result cannot overwrite earlier evidence.

```sh
node prepare.mjs guided guided.intent.json "$SESSION_ID"
node quest.ts guided.intent.json guided.response.json
node prepare.mjs feedback feedback.intent.json "$SESSION_ID"
node quest.ts feedback.intent.json feedback.response.json
node prepare.mjs explain explain.intent.json "$SESSION_ID"
node quest.ts explain.intent.json explain.response.json
node prepare.mjs default default.intent.json "$SESSION_ID"
node quest.ts default.intent.json default.response.json
```

The feedback example includes fictional learner work; Explain includes a supplied solution. These continue the same session and change posture explicitly. `default` omits posture and therefore uses Guided, even after Explain. A client can retain a selected posture by sending it on every turn. `opening` requests a generated opening explicitly; an ordinary first message is preserved as learner input. Setup task and learner preferences are immutable for that session. Support requests ask for `auto`, `hint`, `framework`, `example` or `coaching`; they do not override learning safeguards. `team_dialog` is an optional per-turn boolean.

Attach fictional work with a separate upload. Use PNG/JPEG/WebP up to 8 MiB, 6,000 pixels per side and 36 million pixels, or UTF-8 text/Markdown up to 64 KiB. The server validates type and dimensions. Do not send a data URL in `data`; it is plain base64. There are at most four handles per turn. Uploads expire 30 days after creation, including after reuse or reads.

```sh
node prepare.mjs upload image.intent.json "$SESSION_ID" synthetic-work.png image/png
node quest.ts image.intent.json image.response.json
# Save data.attachment_id as ATTACHMENT_ID, then prepare an ordinary feedback turn:
node prepare.mjs feedback image-feedback.intent.json "$SESSION_ID" "$ATTACHMENT_ID"
node quest.ts image-feedback.intent.json image-feedback.response.json
```

Comma-separated attachment IDs are supported in the last argument. The `quest.attachment_ids` field cannot accompany legacy inline `images`, an opening or closeout. Handles are private to the learner, assignment, region and environment; session-bound uploads cannot move to another session. Do not persist upload bytes in browser operation storage. Uploading and deleting files do not buy a generation.

The transport verifies request/session identity, safety, the closed `quest_receipt`, both public parts and final `done`. Only then does it return a committed answer. Render `parts` with `part: conversation` and `part: display` using safe text/Markdown, with any explicitly requested team dialog separate. Do not extract internal frames from text. A preview or HTTP 200 is insufficient. `quest` describes serving identity, not learning state. Safety status is a separate result; `unknown` is not an all-clear.

If interrupted, retry the exact saved file with a new response filename. This preserves assignment, user, body and idempotency key. Alternatively, prepare `recover` using the original request ID from metadata or the response header. `in_progress` means wait and check the same request. `unavailable` is not permission to purchase another generation. Resolve the original outcome first. A changed body with the same key conflicts.

```sh
node quest.ts guided.intent.json guided-recovery.response.json
node prepare.mjs recover lookup.intent.json "$REQUEST_ID"
node quest.ts lookup.intent.json lookup.response.json
node prepare.mjs end closeout.intent.json "$SESSION_ID"
node quest.ts closeout.intent.json closeout.response.json
node prepare.mjs summary summary.intent.json "$SESSION_ID"
node quest.ts summary.intent.json summary.response.json
```

Closeout generates and saves the summary. Require final completion and `session_ended`. Until a closeout is saved, summary status is `unavailable`. A learner has one active session at a time: opening the learner's next session first closes the open one with a generated closeout, charged as a closeout ($0.05, or one attempt in test mode), the same as calling `end`. Calling `end` is optional; call it when you want the summary saved before the learner's next session. `discard` removes session content without generating closeout. `erase` uses the existing user-erasure operation and needs `data:erase`; do not confuse it with ending a session. The public Learn launch price is $0.05 per turn that succeeds, including opening and closeout, with supported attachments included. Failed uncommitted generation is uncharged; the single internal retry and replay do not add a customer charge. Test mode grants 50 lifetime attempts per workspace and stable Learn listing, shared across members and keys; failed dispatched attempts and closeout count. A test assignment keeps the allowance of the publication it was enrolled on; the console shows that figure and what remains. Reserve an attempt for closeout. Exhaustion never silently switches to live charging. Older private assignments retain their pinned rates.

Other prepared reads: `catalog`, `sessions`, `session SESSION_ID`, `state SESSION_ID`, `history SESSION_ID`, and `profile`. State and profile contain saved observations, not mastery, grades or diagnoses. Empty fields remain unavailable; a read never generates missing evidence. `export` needs `data:export` and returns paged sessions, profile and attachment inventory; `export-file ATTACHMENT_ID` downloads each retained file under the same scope. Follow `next_cursor` by adding it to the saved request's `query` for subsequent pages. Downloads return raw bytes, so choose an appropriate output extension. `download` uses `sessions:read`; `delete-file` is idempotent. Generic `/data/export` remains the full lifecycle export including message history.

For a local browser-to-backend demonstration, prepare a saved intent, then run:

```sh
node server.ts guided.intent.json new-private-receipts
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4317`. The browser sends a same-origin action to its own backend; the backend owns the key, saved body, user and operation ID. The demo permits only that saved intent and writes a new receipt for each explicit replay. It listens on loopback and is not a hosted authentication implementation. A deployed application must bind its authenticated end user and workspace on the server, authorize operations, and persist operation identities before dispatch.

# Your first tutor in ten minutes: what you should see

Run `npm start`, open http://localhost:3000, and ask for help with a problem. For example:

> I'm stuck on 3x + 5 = 20. Can you just tell me what x is?

## The reply

After about 10 to 20 seconds the whole reply appears in two parts:

1. **What the tutor says** (the `conversation` part): a sentence that names what the learner is working on and keeps the step theirs.
2. **The hint to work on** (the `display` part, in Markdown): one question or move that points at the next step. It does not give the value of x.

A real reply, captured November 23, 2026, word for word:

> You’re working with a linear equation and want the value of x. Let’s keep the solving step yours.
>
> In `3x + 5 = 20`, what operation undoes the added 5? Name that operation, then apply it to both sides.

The reply arrives complete and checked. Nothing unchecked is ever shown.

Every reply is written fresh, so yours will use different words. It should still leave the next step to the learner.

## The safety status

Under the reply: **Safety: clear** for an ordinary question. The levels are `clear`, `watch`, `warning` and `critical`; `unknown` means the turn was not evaluated, and is not an all-clear. Step 5 shows how your app acts on each level.

## The receipt

Under the reply, from the turn's final `done` event:

- **1 turn · $0.05 · settled**: one billable unit, 5¢, settled.
- **Request: req_…**: the request id. Keep it; it is how you look a turn up (`GET /v1/requests/<id>`) or ask us about it.

In `receipts.jsonl` on your server, one line per confirmed turn, for example:

```json
{"request_id":"req_…","session_id":"…","learner_id":"learner-…","posture":"guided","safety_level":"clear","billable_units":1,"charge_micro_usd":50000,"settlement":"settled"}
```

## And one thing you should not see

The key. Open your browser's developer tools: the page calls only your own server (`/api/turn`), never the Learn API, and no page or script contains the key.

> You have a specific equation to work with, and you’re asking for the first move. Start by noticing what is being done to the parentheses.
>
> In `2(x - 4) = 10`, what operation is happening to `(x - 4)`? What could you do to both sides to undo that operation?

**Feedback.** A real reply, captured November 23, 2026, word for word:

> You applied distribution, isolated the variable term, and divided to reach a value. I’ll check each line in order and trace the first change that affects the rest.
>
> Your starting equation `2(x - 4) = 10` holds as written. > You translated the equation into successive algebra steps and included a check line. I’ll read each line in order, then trace the first change that affects everything after it.
>
> ### What holds
> - `2(x - 4) = 10` is the equation you were asked to solve.
> - In `2x - 4 = 10`, the `2x` part is carried correctly; the constant term is the part that changes incorrectly.
> - In `2x = 14`, the move of adding the same quantity to both sides is the intended operation, but the value carried into it is off.
> - In `x = 7`, dividing by 2 is the intended final operation, but it is applied to the earlier value.
> - Your check line includes the proposed value and attempts substitution, but it changes the original grouped expression.
> 
> ### First issue
> `2x - 4 = 10` does not hold: this is a distribution error. The 2 must multiply both terms inside the parentheses, so the line should read `2x - 8 = 10`, because `2(x - 4) = 2x - 2(4)`.
> 
> Then continue from that corrected line:
> - `2x - 8 = 10` leads to `2x = 18` after adding 8 to both sides.
> - Dividing both sides by 2 gives `x = 9`.
> 
> Your check, `2(7) - 4 = 10`, does not hold as a check of the original equation: it uses `2x - 4` instead of keeping the parentheses. Using the corrected value in the original form gives `2(9 - 4) = 2 × 5 = 10`.
> 
> Practice keeping the outside factor attached to every term inside parentheses, and preserve the parentheses when substituting into the original equation.

The reply arrives complete and checked. Nothing unchecked is ever shown. Every reply is written fresh, so yours will use different words.

## Under the reply

**Safety: clear**, and the receipt: **1 turn · $0.05 · settled** with the request id. The upload itself was free. `receipts.jsonl` gets one line for the turn.

## What stays private

The photo goes from the page to your server, then to Learn, never straight from the browser to Learn. It belongs to that learner and session, and expires 30 days after upload.

# Step 1: Your first tutor in ten minutes

A chat page where a learner asks for help with a problem and gets a hint from Learn, not the answer. Your server keeps the key; the page talks only to your server.

## You need

- A developer workspace with Learn added, and a server key from **My APIs**.
- Node 24 or later. No packages to install.

## Run it

```sh
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key in .env
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000 and ask for help with a problem, for example "I'm stuck on 3x + 5 = 20. Can you just tell me what x is?"

## What you should see

- After about 10 to 20 seconds, the tutor's reply: a sentence about what you are working on, then a hint that leaves the next step to you.
- Under it, the safety status (for example `Safety: clear`) and the receipt: `1 turn · $0.05 · settled` and the request id.
- A new line in `receipts.jsonl` for each confirmed turn.

## How it works

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `server.ts` | Serves the page, gives each new browser a pseudonymous learner id in a cookie, prepares one Learn session per learner, and relays each turn. |
| `learn.ts` | Calls Learn: `POST /v1/quest/sessions` to prepare a session (free), `POST /v1/chat` for each turn. It accepts a turn only after the final `done` event confirms it. |
| `public/` | The chat page. It shows both parts of each reply: what the tutor says (`conversation`) and the hint to work on (`display`, in Markdown). |

Each turn that succeeds costs 5¢. A turn that fails costs nothing.

This step keeps sessions in memory. If the server restarts, a returning browser gets a new session, and Learn first closes its earlier one: that closeout is billed as its own request, and the first reply takes about ten seconds longer, about 19 seconds. Step 4 keeps sessions on disk.

The integration guide: https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/

## Next

Step 2, **The four kinds of help**, starts from this folder.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Your first tutor with cURL: prepare a session (free), then send one Guided turn
# and read the events Learn sends back. Needs FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY and FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL.
#   bash turn.sh "I am stuck on 3x + 5 = 20. Can you just tell me what x is?"
set -euo pipefail
LEARNER="learner-$(date +%s)-$RANDOM$RANDOM"   # pseudonymous: never a name or an email
MESSAGE="I am stuck on 3x + 5 = 20. Can you just tell me what x is?"
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then MESSAGE="$1"; fi
ASSIGNMENT_HEADER=()
if [ -n "${FOREVERLEARNING_ASSIGNMENT_ID:-}" ]; then ASSIGNMENT_HEADER=(-H "X-Assignment-Id: $FOREVERLEARNING_ASSIGNMENT_ID"); fi

# 1. Prepare a session. Nothing is generated and nothing is charged.
SESSION=$(curl -sS "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/quest/sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY" \
  "${ASSIGNMENT_HEADER[@]}" \
  -H "X-User-Id: $LEARNER" \
  -H "FL-API-Version: 2026-12-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: setup-$LEARNER" \
  --data '{"setup":{"task":{"kind":"homework"},"team_dialog":false}}' \
  | grep -o '"session_id":"[^"]*"' | head -n 1 | cut -d'"' -f4)
echo "Session: $SESSION"

# 2. Send one Guided turn. The reply comes back as server-sent events, complete and checked:
#    metadata, content (conversation, then display), safety_status, quest_receipt, done.
BODY=$(printf '{"session_id":"%s","prompt":"%s","posture":"guided","quest":{"operation":"turn","requested_support":"auto","team_dialog":false}}' \
  "$SESSION" "$(printf '%s' "$MESSAGE" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')")
curl -sS --no-buffer "$FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL/chat" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY" \
  "${ASSIGNMENT_HEADER[@]}" \
  -H "X-User-Id: $LEARNER" \
  -H "FL-API-Version: 2026-12-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: turn-1-$LEARNER" \
  --data "$BODY"

# Step 2: The four kinds of help

One tutor, four kinds of help. On each message the learner chooses:

| Kind | For | How the app asks for it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Guided** | working on a problem | `"posture": "guided"` on the turn |
| **Feedback** | checking finished work | `"posture": "feedback"` on the turn |
| **Explain** | a worked example they don't follow | `"posture": "explain"` on the turn |
| **Diagnostic** | a quiz they finished | a new session prepared with `"posture": "diagnostic"` and the quiz in `setup.assessment`, opened, then answers with no posture |

Guided, Feedback and Explain share one session and change on any turn. Leaving `posture` out means Guided every time, so the app sends it on every turn. Diagnostic is chosen when a session is prepared, with the finished work, so a Diagnostic message starts a session of its own and opens it. Starting a session closes the learner's open one first: that closeout is billed on its own, and the reply takes about ten seconds longer, about 19 seconds.

```sh
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key in .env
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000, choose a kind of help, and send a message. Under each reply: its kind (the receipt's posture), the safety status and the receipt. `receipts.jsonl` keeps one line per turn, with the posture.

# Step 4: Remember the learner

The tutor picks up where the learner left off.

- **Finish for today** ends the session with `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/end`. Learn writes and saves the session's summary and what it learned about the learner. The closeout is a turn.
- Next time, the **Last time** panel shows the saved summary (`GET /v1/quest/sessions/{id}/summary`) and the concepts in the learner's profile, grouped by name (`GET /v1/quest/learners/{id}/profile`). These reads are free; empty evidence stays empty.
- The app keeps its own record of each learner's sessions in `data/learners.json`, so it knows which session is open and which ended.

## Run it

```sh
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key in .env
npm start
```

Ask a question, press **Finish for today**, then open the page again.

Starts from step 3 (`03-photos-of-work`). Next: step 5, **Show the safety status**.

# Step 5: Show the safety status

Every turn carries Learn's safety status: a response action (`none` or `support` on this release; the contract also defines `escalate`) and a level (`clear`, `watch`, `warning`, `critical`, or `unknown` when the turn was not evaluated). Learn has already replied with care, and its reply is shown at once, as Learn wrote it. What your product adds is yours.

| Response action and level | What this app adds, under the reply |
| --- | --- |
| `none`, clear | nothing |
| `support`, watch | a quiet check-in: it's fine to take a break; talk with someone you trust |
| `support`, warning | a support message: it's fine to stop the work; talking with someone you trust can help |
| `support`, critical (or `escalate`) | a help card: please reach out to someone now, with the US crisis line (988) and local emergency numbers elsewhere; an escalation line in the server log |
| `none`, unknown | "This turn couldn't be checked": never treated as clear |

Nothing covers the reply, and the learner never has to press anything to see it. 988 is the US line: Learn is not told where a learner is, so show your own local resources for the other countries you serve, Canada included.

Every turn that is not clear is recorded in `data/safety-events.jsonl` for the people who oversee your app. The escalation line in `server.ts` only logs: to reach a person, connect it to your own on-call, email or messaging, or opt in to the signed safety webhook in the console. Until it really notifies someone, never tell a learner that a person has been told. Your application owns consent, oversight and escalation; adapt the words and the help to your learners and your region.

When a request fails, the page shows the app's own short words (for a message the safety screening refused: "I can't help with that message. Try asking another way."), and Learn's own message goes to the server log.

## Run it

```sh
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key in .env
npm start
```

Starts from step 4 (`04-remember-the-learner`).

# Embed Learn in your app

Learn inside the product you already have, in an afternoon. This folder is the finished example: **Practice Pad**, a small practice product whose help panel now gets its help from Learn. The `start/` folder is the same product before Learn.

## What changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `learn.ts` | New: calls Learn (`POST /v1/quest/sessions`, then `POST /v1/chat` for each turn) and accepts a turn only after the final `done` event confirms it. |
| `learn-route.ts` | New: `POST /api/learn/turn`. Keeps the key, turns your user id into a pseudonymous learner id (a keyed hash), keeps one Learn session per learner, sends the reply to your page when it arrives and keeps every receipt in `receipts.jsonl`. |
| `public/learn-client.js` | New: a drop-in browser module. `askLearn(message, element)` renders the reply (both parts), the safety status and the receipt into any element. |
| `server.ts` | One line mounts the route: `app.use('/api/learn', learnRoute)`. |
| `public/app.js` | The help panel calls `askLearn` instead of the placeholder. |
| `public/style.css` | A few rules for the reply, the safety status and the receipt. |

Your product's look, sign-in and stack stay yours. Learn does the teaching.

## Run it

```sh
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key and a LEARNER_ID_SECRET in .env
npm install
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000 and ask the help panel about a problem.

## What you should see

- After about 10 to 20 seconds, Learn's reply in the help panel: a sentence about what you are working on, then a hint that leaves the next step to you.
- Under it: `Safety: clear`, `Receipt: 1 turn · $0.05 · settled` and the request id.
- One new line in `receipts.jsonl` for each confirmed turn.

Each turn that succeeds costs 5¢. A turn that fails costs nothing.

The sample keeps each learner's session in memory; keep it in your database. If the server forgets an open session, the next one makes Learn close the earlier session first: that closeout is billed as its own request, and the first reply takes about ten seconds longer, about 19 seconds.

The integration guide: https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/learn/
